title: SmoothDriftStronglyConvex.lean

problem_class.label: strongly_convex
problem_class.details: Unconstrained, time-indexed objectives f_k on a real separable Hilbert space. Every f_k is differentiable, μ-strongly convex, has L-Lipschitz gradient, and attains its minimum; 0 < μ ≤ L.

oracle.label: stochastic_gradient
oracle.details: Call k at x returns g_k(x,ω_k), with E[g_k(x,ω_k)] = ∇f_k(x) and E‖g_k(x,ω_k)−∇f_k(x)‖² ≤ σ². Seeds are independent with common law P; the oracle map may vary with k. Each call advances time, so repeated calls cannot query the same time-indexed objective. Public inputs include μ, L, σ, ε and x0; Γ, R, V and H are hidden from algorithm construction.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/SmoothDriftStronglyConvex.lean: Public, Params, spec.publicInput, spec.admissible; LongTails/Setups/StochasticSmoothAndConvex.lean: IsStochasticGradient; LongTails/Template.lean: execute, Convergence.

distinctive_assumptions.label: bounded_variance
distinctive_assumptions.details: Uniform second-moment noise bound σ² at every time and query, with σ ≥ 0; no bounded-support or higher-moment assumption is imposed.

distinctive_assumptions.label: temporal_discrepancy
distinctive_assumptions.details: The minimizer trajectory satisfies ‖x*_0−x0‖ ≤ R, ‖x*_1−x*_0‖ ≤ V, and ‖x*_{k+2}−2x*_{k+1}+x*_k‖ ≤ Γ. There is no uniform bound on subsequent velocities or on temporal gradient variation. With A = 2L/μ + 99σ²/(μ²ε), admissibility requires 9792Γ²A⁴ ≤ ε, where R,V,Γ ≥ 0 and ε > 0.

distinctive_assumptions.label: affine_drift
distinctive_assumptions.details: The allowed case Γ = 0 includes x*_k = x*_0 + kv with unknown, potentially nonzero velocity v satisfying ‖v‖ ≤ V.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/SmoothDriftStronglyConvex.lean: second-difference and initial-velocity conditions in spec.admissible.

accuracy.label: distance_to_solution
accuracy.details: Output (x,N) must satisfy E‖x−x*_{N−1}‖² ≤ ε, with integrable squared error. The output clock starts at zero and increases exactly once per oracle reply; N equals the number of calls made.

accuracy.label: expected
accuracy.details: The squared-distance guarantee averages over both algorithm randomness and independent oracle seeds, at the supplied fixed oracle budget. No high-probability or almost-sure accuracy requirement is imposed.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: This tracking formulation combines one stochastic gradient per advancing time step with hidden minimizer velocity, bounded second differences, an accuracy-dependent acceleration restriction, and expected squared error against the last queried time's minimizer.

descriptionHtml:
Tracking Smooth Strongly Convex Objectives

We consider tracking the minimizers xk⋆ of differentiable functions fk:E→R, indexed by k≥0, on a separable real Hilbert space E. Each objective is μ-strongly convex with L-Lipschitz gradient, where 0<μ≤L. The minimizer path has bounded initial distance from a given point x0∈E, bounded initial velocity, and uniformly bounded second differences. At call k, the oracle returns an unbiased estimate of ∇fk(x) with variance at most σ2, where σ≥0, using a fresh independent sample. For ε>0, the goal is an output (x¯,N) satisfying E∥x¯−xmax{N−1,0}⋆∥2≤ε, where N counts completed calls and expectation covers oracle and algorithm randomness.

The time-indexed optimization problems are minx∈Efk(x),k∈N0. The norm ∥⋅∥ is induced by the inner product on E. The algorithm receives E, the measurable sample space Ω, μ, L, σ, ε, and x0; the parameters Γ,R,V≥0 and H∈N0 may enter only the oracle-call budget. The parameter H imposes no additional condition on the objectives or the minimizer path.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Strong convexity and smoothness). Each fk is Fréchet differentiable everywhere. For every k∈N0 and x,y∈E, fk(y)≥fk(x)+⟨∇fk(x),y−x⟩+μ2∥y−x∥2,∥∇fk(x)−∇fk(y)∥≤L∥x−y∥.

Assumption 2 (Minimizer path and drift). There exists a sequence (xk⋆)k≥0 of global minimizers satisfying fk(xk⋆)≤fk(x)(k≥0, x∈E),∥x0−x0⋆∥≤R,∥x1⋆−x0⋆∥≤V,∥(xk+2⋆−xk+1⋆)−(xk+1⋆−xk⋆)∥≤Γ(k≥0). The drift bound and tolerance satisfy 9792Γ2(2Lμ+99σ2μ2ε)4≤ε.

Assumption 3 (Stochastic gradient oracle). There is a probability measure ν on Ω and, for every k∈N0, a jointly measurable map gk:E×Ω→E. For every fixed x∈E, gk(x,⋅) is Bochner integrable and ∥gk(x,⋅)−∇fk(x)∥2 is integrable under ν, with Eξ∼ν[gk(x,ξ)]=∇fk(x),Eξ∼ν[∥gk(x,ξ)−∇fk(x)∥2]≤σ2. At call k, a query x∈E receives gk(x,ξk), where the samples (ξk)k≥0 are independent with common law ν and are independent of the algorithm’s randomness.

The output includes the number of completed oracle calls. Specifically, its counter starts at c0=0, increases according to ck+1=ck+1 after each reply, and equals the reported value N at termination. Thus the objective advances with each oracle call, and the reported time cannot be chosen independently of the number of calls.

Let P be the joint law of the algorithm’s randomness and the independent oracle samples. After the allotted calls, the output (x¯,N)∈E×N0 must have integrable squared tracking error under P and satisfy EP[∥x¯−xmax{N−1,0}⋆∥2]≤ε. For N≥1, the reference minimizer belongs to the objective queried on the final call; for N=0, it is x0⋆.

theorems.formulaHtml: ⌈16⋅(2⋅Lμ+99⋅σ2μ2⋅ε)⋅log⁡(1+15⋅R2+45⋅V2⋅(2⋅Lμ+99⋅σ2μ2⋅ε)2ε)⌉++H+1

comparisonHtml:
On a separable real Hilbert space, each deterministic fk is differentiable, μ-strongly convex and L-smooth, with 0<μ≤L. Minimizers satisfy ∥x0−x0⋆∥≤R, ∥x1⋆−x0⋆∥≤V and ∥xk+2⋆−2xk+1⋆+xk⋆∥≤Γ. Jointly measurable stochastic gradients use independent samples with common law p, are unbiased and have variance at most σ2 uniformly in x; the relevant first and second moments are integrable. For ε>0 and R,V,Γ,σ≥0, admissibility requires 9792Γ2(2L/μ+99σ2/(μ2ε))4≤ε. The target is ∫∥xN(ω)−xN−1⋆∥2dP(ω)≤ε, where P=p⊗N. The setup requires the output time to count oracle calls, not a particular update rule.

Tracking under SmoothDriftStronglyConvex.
Result Oracle complexity Novelty Limitations
(1) VelocityTrackingSmoothDrift (Ours) (⋆⋆⋆) (review) O(1+H+Alog(1+R2+V2A2ε)) stochastic gradients; every later N succeeds. Updates know μ,L,σ,ε, not Γ,R,V.
(2) SGD with step decay (Cutler et al. 2023), Thms. 4, 28 O(1+κlog(1+R2ε)+σ2μ2ε) gradients to the certified MSE scale ε≍κ2Δ2+(Δσ2/μ2)2/3. Speed-bounded restriction: E∥xk+1⋆−xk⋆∥2≤Δ2; deterministic overlap has V≤Δ, Γ≤2Δ. (1): lower certified error when FΓ≪ε≪(Δσ2/μ2)2/3; every ε>0 if Γ=0. Scope: allows growing speed. No faster cost on the common admissible regime. (1): extra noise logarithm and velocity initialization term; deterministic drift and uniform variance. For Γ≍Δ, requires κ4Δ2 rather than κ2Δ2 accuracy scale.
(3) Romberg NLMS (Moulines et al. 2005), Thm. 8, Cor. 9 No explicit parameter-dependent call budget. MSE O(n−4/5) at smoothness β=2, after a fixed-fraction burn-in; two NLMS updates per sample. Special case: stable time-varying autoregression, smooth coefficients/covariance, bounded innovation and initial moments of order q>8. (1): explicit finite-time extension to nonlinear objectives with arbitrarily changing shape. Matches floor exponent n−4/5 for Γ≍n−2; oracle complexities are not comparable. (1) excludes the multiplicative random-design noise allowed by (3).
(4) Prediction–correction (Kamijima et al. 2025), Thm. 5.5 (q=2) No comparable total-call bound. lim supkE∥x^k−xk⋆∥=O(b+γs+(s+1)h2/5). Requires bounded second trajectory derivative, per-sample strong convexity/smoothness, and correction contracting to sample minimizers with γ∥α∥1<1; history length Θ(h−4/5). (1): finite-time mean square, one fresh gradient per step; removes per-sample convexity and repeated sample solves. The h2/5 rate in (4) requires b=0, γ=O(h2/5). (1) needs variance uniform in x, not just at xk⋆, and excludes convex regularizers. Different oracles and error criteria prevent a cost comparison.

Abbr: κ=L/μ, A=κ+σ2/(μ2ε), FΓ=κ4Γ2+(Γ2σ8/μ8)1/5; H∈N is the supplied horizon slack. MSE: mean-square distance; NLMS: normalized least mean squares; n: sample count in (3). In (4), h is the sampling period, b bounds sample-minimizer bias, s2 bounds its mean-square deviation, γ is the correction contraction factor, and α is the polynomial prediction coefficient vector. ≍ and ≪ denote comparison up to universal factors and asymptotic separation, respectively.

Cutler, Joshua, Dmitriy Drusvyatskiy, and Zaid Harchaoui. 2023. “Stochastic Optimization Under Distributional Drift.” Journal of Machine Learning Research 24 (147): 1–56. https://jmlr.org/papers/v24/21-1410.html.
Kamijima, Tomoya, Naoki Marumo, and Akiko Takeda. 2025. A Regression-Based Prediction-Correction Method for Stochastic Time-Varying Optimization Problems. https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2512.15205.
Moulines, Eric, Pierre Priouret, and François Roueff. 2005. “On Recursive Estimation for Time Varying Autoregressive Processes.” The Annals of Statistics 33 (6): 2610–54. https://doi.org/10.1214/009053605000000624.

import LongTails.Setups.StochasticSmoothAndConvex
import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Basic

open MeasureTheory
open scoped RealInnerProductSpace

namespace LongTails.Setups.SmoothDriftStronglyConvex

open OracleTemplate
open LongTails.Setups.StochasticSmoothAndConvex

structure Public where
  E : Type u
  [normedE : NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [linearE : InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
  [completeE : CompleteSpace E]
  [measurableE : MeasurableSpace E]
  [borelE : BorelSpace E]
  [countableE : SecondCountableTopology E]
  Ω : Type
  [measurableΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω]
  μ : ℝ
  L : ℝ
  σ : ℝ
  ε : ℝ
  x0 : E

attribute [instance] Public.normedE Public.linearE Public.completeE Public.measurableE
  Public.borelE Public.countableE Public.measurableΩ

structure Params extends Public where
  Γ : ℝ
  R : ℝ
  V : ℝ
  H : ℕ

abbrev spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Public
  Instance p := ℕ → p.E → ℝ
  Query p := p.E
  Reply p := p.E
  Output p := p.E × ℕ
  publicInput := Params.toPublic
  valid q := 0 < q.μ ∧ q.μ ≤ q.L ∧ 0 ≤ q.σ ∧ 0 ≤ q.Γ ∧ 0 ≤ q.R ∧ 0 ≤ q.V ∧ 0 < q.ε ∧
    9792 * q.Γ ^ 2 * (2 * q.L / q.μ + 99 * q.σ ^ 2 / (q.μ ^ 2 * q.ε)) ^ 4 ≤ q.ε
  admissible q f O :=
    ∃ (oracle : ℕ → q.E → q.Ω → q.E) (P : ProbabilityMeasure q.Ω),
    O = { Seed := fun _ => q.Ω
          law := ⟨Measure.infinitePi (fun _ : ℕ => (P : Measure q.Ω)), inferInstance⟩
          answer := fun history (_, x) seed => oracle history.length x seed } ∧
    (∀ k, IsStochasticGradient q.E q.Ω P (f k) (oracle k) q.σ) ∧
    (∀ k x, HasGradientAt (f k) (gradient (f k) x) x) ∧
    (∀ k x y, f k x + ⟪gradient (f k) x, y - x⟫ + q.μ / 2 * ‖y - x‖ ^ 2 ≤ f k y) ∧
    (∀ k x y, ‖gradient (f k) x - gradient (f k) y‖ ≤ q.L * ‖x - y‖) ∧
    ∃ xstar : ℕ → q.E, (∀ k, IsMinOn (f k) Set.univ (xstar k)) ∧
      ‖q.x0 - xstar 0‖ ≤ q.R ∧ ‖xstar 1 - xstar 0‖ ≤ q.V ∧
      ∀ k, ‖(xstar (k + 2) - xstar (k + 1)) - (xstar (k + 1) - xstar k)‖ ≤ q.Γ
  successful q f output P :=
    ∃ xstar : ℕ → q.E, (∀ k, IsMinOn (f k) Set.univ (xstar k)) ∧
      Integrable (fun ω => ‖(output ω).1 - xstar ((output ω).2 - 1)‖ ^ 2) (P : Measure _) ∧
      (∫ ω, ‖(output ω).1 - xstar ((output ω).2 - 1)‖ ^ 2 ∂(P : Measure _)) ≤ q.ε
  allowedAlgorithm _ A :=
    ∃ clock : A.State → ℕ, (∀ seed, clock (A.initial seed) = 0) ∧
      (∀ state reply, clock (A.update state reply) = clock state + 1) ∧
      ∀ state, (A.output state).2 = clock state

end LongTails.Setups.SmoothDriftStronglyConvex
